walkthroughs.body_html:
Hamlet's To be or not to be stages philosophical reasoning aloud. The audience hears the workings of conscience and indecision.

Soliloquy is the great Shakespearean instrument of character interiority — without modern access to thought, the convention does that work.

Iago's soliloquies in Othello implicate the audience in his plot — explaining, justifying, taunting. The audience knows the trick well before the victims do.

Dramatic irony reaches its apex when Desdemona pleads ignorance and we already see her death.
An aside is briefer than a soliloquy — a quick remark unheard by other characters. Richard III deploys asides to wink at the audience while charming the court.
